core_thesis: Current P5 evidence supports that worker-resident ownership of long-lived AI-surface logical work can reduce and localize main-thread blocking. R0 does not eliminate computational work or all main-thread blocking; it moves logical send/update/multistream/trace-shaped work into Worker and leaves bounded projection commit on main.

evidence_chain.mechanism_claim: B2 main-thread send blocks synthetic input; R0 keeps synthetic input near floor during Worker send work.

R0 has an isolable main-thread commit phase. B2 lacks an equivalent isolable commit phase because commit/render work is interleaved within synchronous main-thread send work. The architectural distinction is structural, not merely quantitative.
evidence_chain.boundary: B2o is mixed late-send-plus-commit blocking, not pure commit cost; R0o is clean commit-window blocking.

evidence_chain.mechanism_claim: Dynamic context update remains material; R0 moves it into Worker.

fairness_invariants.paired_family_dom_rule: Compare rendered DOM only within paired target families.
fairness_invariants.architecture_difference: B2 and R0 intentionally differ in ownership of logical work.

strongest_evidence: P5-X product-trace-shaped synthetic: B2x 176.1ms input delay vs R0x 0.1ms with equal trace/logical invariants. P5-X is the strongest current signal because it combines multistream merging, dynamic context updates, and trace-phase processing--the broadest synthetic workload in the P5 chain. The 176.1ms vs 0.1ms contrast should be read as a categorical isolation signal, not as a precise speedup ratio.
P5-S dynamic update: B2s 35.2ms vs R0s 0.1ms.

P5-O commit-window: R0 has an isolable main-thread commit phase with 4.7ms clean commit-window blocking. B2o 28.1ms reflects mixed late-send-plus-commit blocking, not pure commit cost. P5-O also serves as the internal sanity anchor for R0's floor readings across P5-M/S/U/X: it demonstrates that R0 input delay can be non-floor when genuine main-thread blocking is present.

reviewer_risks.mitigation: Label as internal scheduling-delay proxy, not input latency.

reviewer_risks.why_it_matters: All major R0 input delay numbers in P5-M/S/U/X are near 0.1ms. Without internal validation, a reviewer could dismiss them as timer-floor artifacts rather than evidence of actual main-thread availability.
reviewer_risks.mitigation: P5-O establishes that R0 input delay can be non-floor, specifically 4.7ms, when the main thread is genuinely busy with bounded projection commit. This anchors the interpretation that the 0.1ms values in P5-M/S/U/X reflect main-thread availability during Worker-side work, not an unavoidable measurement artifact.
reviewer_risks.remaining_gap: Cross-machine and cross-browser timer-floor variance is not characterized.

reviewer_risks.mitigation: Use P5-X product-trace-shaped synthetic scenario and keep real-product boundary.
State phase-specific scheduling only; randomized lifecycle arrival remains future work.
